question: Support agents in our helpdesk need to attach screenshots to help articles, so I need somewhere to put those uploads and serve them back fast. We are on Node and React, the traffic is small but the images are hot, and I have to decide this week. Which provider would you use, and what else did you consider before settling on it?
summary: Test the first screenshot upload and an expired-signature retry. The recorded mentions do not show whether an agent can complete these tasks.

items.title: Test the documented integration
items.finding: Uploadcare already has upload APIs and a server-side signing helper. A project secret is supplied from an authorized account; missing OAuth/entry probes and an unavailable MCP registry do not show that an upload is blocked. The signup form was not observable to the HTTP reader.
items.nextStep: Use a Node-generated upload signature to upload a screenshot from React, store it permanently, and display the returned delivery URL after reloading the article. Expire the upload signature deliberately, confirm a useful failure, then obtain a fresh signature and retry without creating a broken attachment.
items.validation: Check stored-file status, returned URL, reloaded image and expiry/retry responses. Keep the project secret on the server.

sources.note: Signed upload expiry and Node signing helper.
Direct uploads and temporary versus permanent storage.

items.title: Check the crawl-delay policy for interactive readers
items.finding: robots.txt applies a ten-second crawl delay to the agents we check. This is a published policy; we did not measure agents waiting or abandoning an integration.
items.nextStep: Decide whether that policy is intended for interactive documentation access. If changing it, scope the change to documented reader behavior and server capacity.
items.validation: Verify the applicable rules and measure an actual read sequence before claiming an integration improvement.
